General prior (not SPIDER evidence): repeated pre-freeze design-stage failures under one control revision are a process/substrate signal, not evidence about the scientific hypothesis; the correct response is to repair the shared blocker once and PARK the thread on the specific dependency rather than re-discover the same absence as per-lane invalids.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): stored selectors and paths rot silently - the costly failure is wrong-target resolution that still reports success - so resolution/freshness guards must be judged on false accepts and abstention calibration (UNKNOWN precision), not on loud misses.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): long-horizon agent failures are dominated by path-dependent subplanning errors and loss of durable state, which is the mechanism-level reason inheritance can pay only if it reduces residual novelty and re-establishes verified state - favoring mechanism-level semantic resolution + verification over full-route replay.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): an experiment whose success and failure branches change no current decision should not consume a cycle; a cheap probe that varies the single factor an accepted result fixed has value only while a downstream decision is actually waiting on it.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): an external vanilla actor or vendor-native cache can already replay and self-heal; market-level moat claims require competitor-strength controls, and four internal arms alone cannot establish a competitive advantage.

allocation.rationale: Decision counterfactual: if a soundness certification step (e.g., declarations derived from an audited closed-world origin, or an adversarial partially-observable-declaration test that fires on over-wide declarations) holds zero false accepts, the shipped carrier can safely ingest external declarations - closing the single largest open safety boundary on B1's shipped artifact and preparing the SPIDER arm of the flagship benchmark to consume mechanisms; if soundness is not certifiable, the product decision is a documented closed-world trust boundary (UNKNOWN over unsafe execution), which is itself a decisive product answer. Strongest fair baseline: the current shipped conservative fallback (coverage 0.675, zero false accepts) plus the measurement-valid declared-guard results from EXP-PRODUCT-38201227093; improvement must be a strict safe-coverage gain, never a false-accept regression. Validity/dependency: the regression gate and adversarial declaration bank must be frozen pre-freeze; the BP-DECL-OVERWIDE negative is adopted and must not be re-litigated or re-run. Budget/stopping: smallest decisive batch is one shipped kernel change + one regression/adversarial certificate + one declared-soundness certification step (or its impossibility receipt); stop rule: do NOT re-run the promotion certificate (EXP-PRODUCT-38180719830) or the observational-widening negative (EXP-PRODUCT-38197856050), and stop if the guard cannot be implemented without regressing the shipped zero-false-accept boundary. Cognitive reset: with today's Codex and no handoff, Product would ask what most threatens the shipped carrier's safe use by external agents - declaration soundness is the open boundary named by the lane's own last packet; the alternative (harness stand-up) produces no evidence while B2/B3 are open, so this direction wins.
